title: Output fragmentation and rate-signal regression — incident follow-up
creator: Aisha Raman
description: This ticket tracks the investigation and remediation for a production regression that caused fragmented streaming responses: partial token fragments, early stream termination for some clients, and increased reconnects. The behaviour first appeared after a serving runtime optimization (queued kernel pre-flush) rolled to canary and then production. We need to record findings, prioritize fixes, and ship guardrails and tests to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: Between 2026-03-03T09:10Z and 2026-03-03T13:40Z a subset (~0.8%) of streaming sessions experienced truncated token sequences or token-fragment boundary splits leading to client-side parse errors and reconnect loops. Errors peaked following a deploy that introduced a new rate-signal heuristic intended to improve batching for short tail latency. The deploy changed flush thresholds which, combined with HTTP chunking behavior on our proxy, caused mid-token chunk boundaries to be emitted to clients.

root_cause_hypothesis: A regression in the rate-signal/batching heuristic introduced a pre-flush path that sometimes emitted incomplete byte sequences for a token when combined with the proxy's chunking logic. The runtime assumed token-level atomicity at the emission boundary; however the proxy flushes at network-chunk granularity, exposing mid-codepoint boundaries. This is exacerbated by an optimization that reduces per-request buffering to lower tail latency, which reduced the chance buffer contains a complete multi-byte token before flush.
